risk_analysis.author: risk-analyst
risk_analysis.method: Knowledge-only (cutoff Jan 2026). Regulatory posture (DPF status, sub-processor lists, contract terms) must be re-verified against vendor DPAs and trust pages before signature.

gdpr_posture.salesforce: EU residency available via Hyperforce (EU Operating Zone adds EU-located support and ops at extra cost). US parent: FISA 702 / CLOUD Act reachability persists regardless of residency. EU-US Data Privacy Framework certified; SCCs as fallback. Long, well-documented sub-processor list (hyperscaler infra underneath Hyperforce). Mature DPA, strong audit/certification stack (ISO 27001/27701, SOC 2). Residual transfer risk: LOW-MODERATE.
gdpr_posture.hubspot: EU data hosting in Frankfurt (AWS eu-central-1) must be selected AT PORTAL CREATION — existing US portals cannot simply be relocated, so get this right on day one. US parent, DPF-certified, SCCs in DPA; some support and product telemetry access can originate from the US/other regions. Sub-processor transparency is good. Residual transfer risk: LOW-MODERATE.
gdpr_posture.zoho: EU customers served from Zoho-owned Amsterdam + Dublin data centres (no hyperscaler dependency — a genuine plus). Parent is Indian (no EU adequacy decision): any India-based support/engineering access relies on SCCs, and Zoho's sub-processor and audit documentation is thinner than the other two. DPA adequate but less battle-tested with EU regulators. Residual transfer risk: MODERATE.
gdpr_posture.shared_assumption: DPF remains valid as of Jan 2026 but is litigation-exposed (Schrems-pattern challenge risk); SCC fallback plus EU residency keeps all three viable for an Irish controller. Brightline holds client/prospect B2B contact data, not special-category data, so risk ceiling is inherently moderate.

lock_in_and_exit.salesforce: Highest lock-in: proprietary customisation layer (Apex, Flow, metadata) does not port; multi-year non-cancellable orders are standard; data egress is easy (APIs, weekly export) but PROCESS egress is expensive — expect EUR 15-40k to rebuild workflows elsewhere.
lock_in_and_exit.hubspot: Moderate: clean CSV/API export for CRM objects, but marketing workflows, email assets, and attribution history do not migrate; annual prepaid terms with auto-renewal uplift clauses — diarise renewal windows.
lock_in_and_exit.zoho: Lowest contractual lock-in (monthly/annual, modest sums), BUT the Zoho One bundle is an operational lock-in trap: once email, finance and projects ride on it, exit cost multiplies across the business. Keep scope CRM-only initially.

risk_analysis.migration_risk: Inbound migration (assumed: spreadsheets/legacy lightweight CRM) is low-complexity for all three. Salesforce realistically requires a partner (adds EUR 15-40k, already modelled). HubSpot has the best guided import tooling. Zoho is fine technically but the thin Irish partner pool means slower rescue if migration goes sideways. Largest migration risk is human: 40 creatives abandoning the tool → CRM becomes stale within a quarter. Severity highest for Salesforce (admin burden), lowest for HubSpot.

hidden_cost_risk.salesforce: ~9% list-price rise cadence (2023, 2025 — assume it recurs), paid add-ons for ad-ops (Account Engagement, Data Cloud), Premier Support ~30% uplift, plus a part-time admin or partner retainer (EUR 10-25k/yr). Realistic 3-yr TCO is 1.5-2x the headline EUR 79.2k/yr.
hidden_cost_risk.hubspot: Marketing-contact tier creep is the big one: costs scale with database size, not seats — agencies that import prospect lists hit tier jumps fast (the EUR 9.5-19k/yr add-on estimate can double). Custom objects/advanced reporting gated to Enterprise (~EUR 150/seat). Mandatory onboarding fee (~EUR 1.5-3k).
hidden_cost_risk.zoho: Headline price is honest, but gap-filling is the cost: middleware (reverse-ETL/Zapier/Make) for Meta and programmatic sync, developer time for API work, and persistent Zoho One upsell pressure. Budget EUR 5-10k/yr for glue.

support_risk.salesforce: Standard support is slow; meaningful SLAs require Premier (paid). Excellent Irish partner ecosystem (EMEA presence in Dublin). Risk LOW if partner retainer accepted, else MODERATE.
support_risk.hubspot: EMEA HQ is literally in Dublin; phone/chat support included at Pro tier; deepest local agency-partner bench. Risk LOW — best of the three for Brightline.
support_risk.zoho: Support routed via EU/India mix, premium support costs ~20-25% extra, and the Irish partner/talent pool is thin (flagged in stage 1). Risk MODERATE-HIGH: Brightline would be largely self-reliant.

risk_register.risk: US government access to EU-hosted data (FISA 702 / CLOUD Act) despite Hyperforce residency
risk_register.mitigation: EU Operating Zone option; DPF + SCCs in DPA; data minimisation — keep only B2B contact data in CRM.

risk_register.risk: Admin/configuration burden overwhelms a 40-person agency; adoption collapses
risk_register.mitigation: Only proceed with a partner retainer + named internal admin; otherwise eliminate from shortlist.

risk_register.risk: Compounding ~9% list-price rises + add-on dependency (Data Cloud, Account Engagement) inflate 3-yr TCO 1.5-2x
risk_register.mitigation: Multi-year price-lock and add-on pricing caps negotiated pre-signature; model 3-yr TCO not year-1.

risk_register.risk: Process lock-in: proprietary automations make future exit a EUR 15-40k rebuild
risk_register.mitigation: Document all workflows tool-agnostically; quarterly full data exports; avoid Apex where Flow suffices.

risk_register.risk: Marketing-contact tier creep — cost scales with database size, can double the marketing add-on
risk_register.mitigation: Contractual contact-tier pricing schedule up-front; quarterly list hygiene; mark non-marketing contacts (free) correctly.

risk_register.risk: EU (Frankfurt) hosting must be chosen at portal creation; later relocation is effectively a re-implementation
risk_register.mitigation: Specify EU data residency in the order form; verify portal region before any data import.

risk_register.risk: Feature ceiling: custom objects and advanced reporting gated to Enterprise, forcing a ~EUR 150/seat upgrade later
risk_register.mitigation: Validate reporting requirements against Pro tier in trial; pre-price the Enterprise delta in negotiation.

risk_register.risk: Renewal auto-uplift on annual prepaid contracts
risk_register.mitigation: Cap renewal uplift (CPI or fixed %) in the order form; calendar the renewal notice window.

risk_register.risk: India-parent data transfers (support/engineering access) rest on SCCs without an adequacy decision; thinner sub-processor transparency
risk_register.mitigation: Request EU-only support handling in the DPA; complete a TIA; confirm Amsterdam/Dublin residency in writing.

risk_register.risk: Thin Irish partner and admin-talent pool — slow rescue when integrations or migration stall
risk_register.mitigation: Identify and pre-qualify a UK/EU Zoho partner before contract; keep an internal power-user trained.

risk_register.risk: Ad-ops gaps (Meta, programmatic) require DIY middleware — hidden EUR 5-10k/yr glue cost and fragility
risk_register.mitigation: Pilot the Meta sync path during trial; budget middleware explicitly; treat failure as a deal-breaker for an ad agency.

risk_register.risk: Zoho One bundle adoption converts cheap CRM into business-wide operational lock-in
risk_register.mitigation: Constrain scope to CRM-only for 12 months; require a written exit/export test before any bundle expansion.

risk_register.risk: DPF invalidation (Schrems-pattern litigation) disrupts US-parent transfer basis
risk_register.mitigation: Ensure SCCs are the contractual fallback in every DPA; EU residency already limits primary-data exposure.

risk_register.risk: All pricing is Jan-2026 knowledge-cutoff list pricing; actuals may differ
risk_register.mitigation: Pre-contract verification of vendor pricing pages and a written quote is a mandatory gate before recommendation sign-off.

risk_analysis.ranking_impact: Risk analysis CONFIRMS the preliminary ranking HubSpot > Zoho > Salesforce. HubSpot's dominant risks (contact-tier creep, renewal uplift) are contract-mitigable; its GDPR and support posture are the best fit for a Dublin agency. Zoho stays second: the cost case is real, but ad-ops gap-filling and support self-reliance are recurring taxes, and GDPR diligence is heavier. Salesforce carries the highest composite risk (adoption 4, cost-creep 4, lock-in 3) for capability Brightline does not yet need.
